findings: The 113-part installed reference retains the original 62-part tripod and exact rigid source shapes, transformed without scale. Three distinct guy assemblies and a separate grounding lead are visible.

Upper-eye and turnbuckle views show each continuous guy wire returning through the two real clamp channels, including the selected 25 mm free tails. The lower close-up shows separate turnbuckle eyes, perpendicular S hook and stake head.
The foot close-up shows the smaller stake passing through an existing foot-plate hole. All six stakes and the ground rod enter soil outside the candidate hard paths and pads.

Ground close-ups show one continuous lead from the mast saddle groove to the rod-clamp bore, with visible free ends. The selected route consumes 0.2930400109284107 m from the selected 3 m stock; three guys consume 10.520065666817535 m from the source 15.24 m stock.
The broad view retains separate earthen ground, ordinary paths and bench pads. This is a standalone alternative state; the original main laboratory has not been replaced.
geometry_limits: Static authored installed poses do not establish an executable assembly sequence, ground strength, tension, thread engagement, retention, electrical continuity or robot use.
Wire lengths are centreline measurements with ideal zero cutting loss. The loose uncut kit and cut-wire reference are alternative states, not simultaneous inventory.

Local source vertices and separate scene transforms preserve small geometry during float32 export. Pairwise overlap tests recenter meshes near the tested contact; no rigid-part scale change or world-fixed attachment is used.
Ground top inspection omits soil to expose subsurface hardware. All local fixture profiles, route curvature, selected wire diameters and clamp gaps remain disclosed hypotheses.
Attached wind and temperature sensors, logger connections, level, initial staging and complete human-scale working clearances remain pending.
